name: Cohen-Gibson syndrome
aliases: overgrowth and intellectual disability syndrome, EED type

clinicalPearls: Caused by heterozygous variants in EED, which encodes a core subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2), the chromatin-modifying complex responsible for trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 27
Presents as a Weaver-like overgrowth syndrome, with tall stature, macrocephaly and advanced bone age accompanying intellectual disability
Facial features overlap those of Weaver syndrome, including a broad forehead, hypertelorism, large ears and a small chin

Because Weaver syndrome (EZH2), Cohen-Gibson syndrome (EED) and Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome (SUZ12) all disrupt PRC2, they form a clinically overlapping spectrum distinguished mainly by the gene involved
Skeletal manifestations may include advanced osseous maturation, camptodactyly and other limb anomalies
As PRC2 dysfunction relaxes epigenetic silencing of growth-promoting genes, tumour surveillance is considered, mirroring the malignancy risk debated in related PRC2 overgrowth disorders
Diagnosis relies on molecular identification of a pathogenic EED variant, often supported by a recognisable overgrowth episignature where testing is available
reference.pathophysiology: EED encodes an essential scaffolding component of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2, a multiprotein assembly that, through its catalytic partner EZH2, deposits the repressive histone mark H3K27me3 to silence target genes during development. Pathogenic EED variants impair the complex's ability to establish or read this mark, reducing repression of genes that promote cellular proliferation and growth. The resulting loss of appropriate transcriptional silencing manifests as generalised overgrowth, accelerated skeletal maturation and disordered neurodevelopment, and because the same complex is affected in Weaver and Imagawa-Matsumoto syndromes these conditions share a common mechanistic basis and overlapping features.
additionalInvestigations: Exome or genome sequencing to identify pathogenic EED variants
DNA methylation episignature analysis where a validated overgrowth signature is available
Bone age radiograph to document advanced skeletal maturation
Growth charting with serial head circumference measurement
Brain MRI if structural anomalies or seizures are suspected
Clinical surveillance for tumours in keeping with practice for related PRC2 overgrowth disorders
redFlags: Disproportionate or accelerating overgrowth prompting review for an embryonal or other tumour
New abdominal mass or unexplained pain warranting imaging
Rapidly enlarging head circumference or neurological deterioration
Severe feeding difficulty or hypotonia in infancy
reference.prognosis: Long-term data are limited because of rarity, but children typically show persistent overgrowth with intellectual disability of variable severity; life expectancy is not clearly reduced in the absence of malignancy, and management centres on developmental support, orthopaedic monitoring and vigilance for tumours as advised for the wider PRC2 overgrowth group.
pitfalls: Attributing the overgrowth solely to Sotos or Weaver syndrome without gene-specific testing across the PRC2 group
Neglecting tumour surveillance considerations that apply to PRC2-related overgrowth
Overlooking advanced bone age as a diagnostic clue
Assuming normal cognition because overgrowth dominates the presentation
references: Nature Reviews — Polycomb repressive complexes in development and disease
management: No disease-specific therapy; care is supportive and multidisciplinary, centred on developmental and educational support for intellectual disability
Orthopaedic monitoring and management of skeletal manifestations including camptodactyly, advanced bone age and limb anomalies
Serial growth and head-circumference charting to track the overgrowth phenotype
Tumour surveillance given the debated malignancy risk shared across PRC2-related overgrowth syndromes
Neurodevelopmental and cognitive assessment guiding therapies, with brain MRI where structural anomalies or seizures arise
Genetic counselling for this heterozygous EED (PRC2) disorder, which is typically de novo, with confirmatory sequencing and family testing
